newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore passes anti-dumping duties law.
newsitem.headline: Singapore passes anti-dumping duties law.

text.p: Singapore on Tuesday passed the Countervailing and Anti-Dumping Duties Act to bring existing laws in line with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreement.

Trade and industry minister Yeo Cheow Tong said that as a WTO member, Singapore needs to update the 1962 Customs (Dumping and Subsidies) Act to meet the country's commitments under the WTO agreements.
Countervailing duties are import duties imposed over and above normal levels when an importing country considers the export price to contain a subsidy.
The changes clearly define key terms and definitions in the previous Act such as what constitutes domestic industry, the scope of interested parties and what are considered "like goods".
The amendments also include detailed provisions to ensure transparency and consistency in the procedures for anti-dumping and countervailing actions.
Yeo said while Singapore remains committed to free trade, it is entitled to take action against unfair trade practices which can cause damage to domestic producers.
